sentences.text: 1 This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 29.12.2023 at about 2.10 p.m, the petitioner was traveling in the bus bearing No.KA-18-B-5669 from the starting point.
The driver of the bus driven the same in a rash and negligent manner.
The passengers of the bus told the driver to go slow.
In spite of repeated request made by the passengers to the driver to go slow but he had not heard.

When the said bus so proceeding near Marasinge Village, Kalasa Taluk, Chikkamagaluru District, at that time the bus driver abruptly took a sudden turn with high speed, due to heavy jerk,
the petitioner thrown out from the bus and sustained grievous injuries.
It is further urged that immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Kalasa Government hospital and after first aid he was shifted to Hassan Government Hospital.
Thereafter he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as inpatient and underwent surgery.
It is also urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent act of the driver of Bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 18-B-5669.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.2, the respondent No.2 did not interested appear before this Tribunal.

Hence he placed exparte.
4.
After service of notice, respondent No.1 filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent admitted the issuance of package insurance policy in respect of vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-18-B-5669.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.

Non -compliance of section's 134(c),
158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.

This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence,
mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Further negligence on the part of the driver of its insured vehicle is denied.
Per contra it is alleged that the petitioner traveling on the foot board of the bus, hence the compensation if any awarding the petitioner is to be contributed to 50% the accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 29.12.2023 at about 2.10 pm., when he was standing near the door and traveling in the bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 18-B-5669, near Marasinge Village, Kalasa Taluk, Chikkamagaluru District at that time driver of said bus drove the same in high speed in abruptly took sudden turn and due to heavy jerk he has thrown out from the bus.
As a result of forced impact, he was sustained grievous injuries as alleged?

Shankar Rao vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36770753/
2 2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

entities.text: Shankar Rao vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
6.
The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 14 were marked on his behalf.

Dr.Shekar. M.,
Orthopedic Surgeon was examined as PW.2.
Ex's .P15 to 17 were marked through him.
The respondents did not choose to lead any evidence on its behalf.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.1 counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:
The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.20 lakhs together.
The petitioner has mainly relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7 being police documents.

On careful perusal of these documents it appears that based on the information given by petitioner himself the Kalasa Police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 and investigated the matter and submitted the charge sheet as per Ex.P.7.
In order to prove the factum of negligence the petitioner has mainly relied on Ex.P.3, Ex.P.4 and Ex.P.7 charge sheet.
This Court gave anxious consideration on astuteness to the contents of the above said document.

On conspectus reading of Ex.P.3 and 4 it reflects that the accident happened near Marasinge village, Kalasa Taluk,
Chikkamagaluru District.
Further on careful perusal of Ex.P.3 Crime Details form it clearly depicts that the said road is curve road and the accident happened at the edge of the road.

On close perusal of the same it reflects that, the driver of the Bus in which the petitioner was proceeding as passenger / inmate, the driver drove the same in high speed and due to heavy jerk, the petitioner thrown out from the bus and caused the accident.
If the driver of the bus was coming in a normal speed then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Above all even the charge sheet was also filed as against the driver of the bus for the offences punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC and u/s 177 of IMV Act.
This Court is aware of the fact that charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the Ex.P.3 which was read in consonance with the Ex.P.7 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is an rash and negligent act of the driver of the bus.

10. Though the respondent No.1 contended that the insured vehicle is not at all involved in the accident but in order to substantiate the same absolutely no materials placed on record by respondent No.1.
Mere self serving and self proclaimed statement is not trump card for success of the case of respondent No.1.

Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P.7 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this Court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents Shankar Rao vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36770753/
3 prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle.

sentences.text: Consequently this tribunal hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the bus.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
11. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the bus.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.
12. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :

The petitioner has exhibited her Aadhar card at Ex.P10,
wherein his date of birth is reflected as 18.02.1966.
This indicates that he was aged (57 years 10 months 12 days) 58 years on the date of accident.
13. The petitioner deposed that prior to the accident she was working as driver and getting an salary of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
In order to substantiate the said fact he has not produced any documents to prove the same.

It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA. No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.
05.07.2023.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 29.12.2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.
14. As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : Pain and swelling over left and right leg and left shoulder.
It is needless to say that the injuries are grievous in nature.

The discharge summary of Sanjay Gandhi Hospital indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient from 30.12.2023 to 21.01.2024 (23 days) and from 11.07.2024 to 25.07.2024 (15) days, in total the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital for a period of 38 days.

During the course of treatment she had undergone surgeries in the form of : CRIF with IMIL Nail for left tibia with ORIF with plating for left fibula, ORIF with plates and screws for right fibula and ankle spanning Ex-Fix, Reduction and conservative management with shoulder immobilizer for left shoulder dislocation.

Further implant removal of fibular plate ORIF with plates and screws for fibula replating done ORIF with plate and screws for right tibia with iliac bone grafting done on Shankar Rao vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36770753/
4 20.07.2024 under SAB.
15.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is the specific case of the petitioner that, owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.Shekar. M as PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained total permanent physical disability of 55.85% to right lower limb, 16.71% to left lower limb and 31.09% disability to the whole body.
It is elicited during the course of cross examination PW.2 categorically admitted that he was treated the petitioner.
Further he also advised to follow up treatment to the petitioner.
Further he admitted that in both discharge summaries it is mentioned as condition during discharge is improved.
He categorically admitted that at the time of assessment of disability the fractures are united.
When such is the case physical disability assessed by the medical expert is on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctors, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 18%, cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, I consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 18%.
16. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES : The period of hospitalization of 38 days is proved with a help of discharge summary.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/- per day and a sum of Rs.45,600/- (1,200 X 38) is awarded under this head.
17. PAIN & SUFFERINGS : On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.80,000/- under this head.
18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of her stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 4 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards Rs.64,000/- (16,000 X 4) under this head.
19. MEDICAL EXPENSES :

As per the bills marked at Ex.P12, the petitioner has spent Rs.41,812/-
and Ex.P.14 Rs.7,392/- towards medical expenses.
During the course of cross examination PW.1 admitted that he is having BPL Card.
He further admitted that he has produced advance receipts and not produced the inpatient bill.
He further admitted that the inpatient bills are not found in records.
He admitted that in Ex.P.12 Advance receipts it is mentioned in billing type column as BPL.

Further during the course of cross-examination of PW.2 he admitted that their hospital provides benefits to BPL cardholders and under the Ayushman Bharat Scheme, and the government has Shankar Rao vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36770753/
5 borne Rs.25,000 accordingly.

sentences.text: Hence Sl.No.1 and 2 of Ex.P.12 are not considered and rest of the bills amount is granted.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for (Rs.26,812/- + Rs.7,392/- = Rs.34,204/-
which is rounded off to Rs.34,200/- towards medical expenses.
20. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '9'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.3,11,040/- (Rs.16,000 X 12 X 9 X 18/100) which is rounded off to Rs.3,11,000/- is awarded under this head.
21. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of her life.
Hence a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded under this head.
22. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The doctor witness stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants for which she may require Rs.25,000/-.

On perusal of Ex.P.8 discharge summary wherein he took treatment from 11.07.2024 to 25.07.2024, it is clearly mentioned that the petitioner underwent implant removal of fibular plate ORIF with plates and screws for fibula replating done ORIF with plate and screws for right tibia with Iliac bone grafting done on 20.07.2024.
Hence it is clear that implants removal surgery already done, hence the petitioner is not entitled any compensation under this.

23. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra : 45,600-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 2 Pain & sufferings : 80,000-00 3 Loss of income during laid-up : 64,000-00 period 4
Medical expenses : 34,200-00 5 Loss of future income due to : 3,11,000-00 disability 6 Loss of future amenities & : 50,000-00 happiness 7

Future medical expenses : - Nil -
Total 5,84,800-00 24.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
25. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-18-B-5669 and respondent No.2 being the owner thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable Shankar Rao vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36770753/
6 to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

26. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,84,800/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
